The snippets collectively show two complementary facets: multiple sources report that some penguin species live and thrive in warm climates, while others emphasize that cold-adapted species are challenged by warmth. d3 and d5 explicitly affirm warm-weather survival for many species, d7 and d2 note species outside icy habitats, and d4 and d6 acknowledge that cold specialists can overheat or fail in prolonged warmth. Yes. Some penguin species can survive in warm weather, with about 14 species currently living in warm regions; they use behavioral adaptations such as stretching flippers, shading feet, panting, and seeking cooler microhabitats to regulate body temperature [d3]. Other sources note that penguins occur beyond Antarctica and can be comfortable in temperatures 100 degrees above zero, including species like Humboldts in Hawaii, further supporting warm-weather survival for certain penguins [d5, d7]. At the same time, cold-adapted species like Emperor penguins can overheat on land and rely on cooling mechanisms, indicating that not all penguins thrive in prolonged warmth [d4].
